findings.title: TLS certificate has expired
findings.explanation: The site's SSL/TLS certificate has already expired, causing certificate verification failures when connecting securely. Visitors' browsers will show scary warnings telling them the site is not safe, which drives people away and can look like a hack to customers.
findings.recommendation: Renew the TLS certificate immediately and confirm the new certificate installs correctly on the web server, ideally with auto-renewal configured going forward.

findings.title: No DMARC record found
findings.explanation: The domain has an SPF record but no DMARC record. Without DMARC, it's easier for scammers to send emails that appear to come from this domain, which can be used for phishing against customers or employees.
findings.recommendation: Publish a DMARC TXT record (starting with a monitoring policy like p=none, then tightening it) for the domain.

findings.title: Core security headers are properly configured
findings.explanation: The site sends Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, and Referrer-Policy headers, which is a good baseline defense against common web attacks like clickjacking and content sniffing.
findings.recommendation: No action needed; keep these headers in place when making future server changes.
